touches.text: Sleep is one of those scheduled things. At its time Cairn kicks off sleep by running its own sleep routine, then hands the sleep token over the bus to the next device, and so on. The rack's order is the token's order (5.6.2.3).
Sleep's base trigger is the clock (2300). Once we can tell how recently things were interacted with, that overrides the base clock. (Q#10, Akien 2026-11-03)

When this box may be used is decided from three inputs. The schedule sets a baseline. Observing Akien (how recently things were interacted with) can open time that would otherwise not exist: measuring trumps rules. An away window ("going to bed", "out to the theater", x to y) does the same.

The sleep token goes round in sequence, one sleeper at a time, so that no one sleeper takes the whole system to everyone else's cost. The order itself doesn't matter: it is alphabetical by device, then by instance. That is the same on every box and needs nothing stored. (Q#17, Akien 2026-11-04; alphabetical is CC's pick)

Processes the sleep cycle, if its device needs one: when the sleep token arrives, it wakes its device to do its sleep (the device does the sleeping, not the shim), then passes the token on. If its device won't come up, the shim files the trouble and still passes the token on, so the rest of the rack sleeps.
scheduler (part of the base shim, 5.7; was sleep_cycle): uses tools base, rack
Sleep is one entry on Cairn's list. Its routine runs Cairn's own sleep, then hands the token to the first device in the rack.
